messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: High error rate & OOMs on kv-cache pool (region: us-west-2). 5xx spike + CUDA malloc failures observed. auto-escalate to oncall.

sara (oncall): I’m on it. seeing alert dashboard -> eviction_rate x6, batch latency spikes. Which service first?

leo (eng-runtime): kv-cache-contbatch service (dedicated pool) started showing repeated arena resizes and slab fragmentation. Logs show repeated `pytorch::cuda::malloc` failures and `KVCache::slot_alloc` retries.

anya (eng-sre): tagging logs: https://logs.redwood.internal/streams/kv-cache?from=3109876400 - throwing OOMs at ~3109876502. Also seeing continuous-batching loop attempting to coalesce giant prefixes -> batch sizes jumped to 12k tokens in some requests.

matt (ml-infra): That batch size jump smells like the new batching heuristic merge from last deploy. Canary toggles?

leo (eng-runtime): Correct — new contbatch heuristic (PR #488) shipped in last canary. It aggressively merges by prefix similarity, didn't bound combined token count. Result: huge KV caches/k-v entries live -> fragmentation over time -> slow cuda malloc -> OOM.

anya (eng-sre): Customer impact: four active tenants showing degraded tail latency, a couple 5xx. Pierre, CS, do you have any escalations?

pierre (customer-success): One enterprise contact reported increased API error rates and latency >2s for embeddings. They raised a ticket. Expect an SLA conversation if not mitigated in 2h.

sara (oncall): Triage plan: 1) Stop the contbatch heuristic by toggling runtime flag. 2) Apply batch size caps. 3) Roll small hotfix to allocator thresholds / arena tuning if needed. 4) Drain worst nodes.

leo (eng-runtime): Running command to flip feature flag on production pool (targeting us-west-2 canary group first):
```
# feature flag toggle
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" \
  https://controlplane.redwood.internal/api/flags/contbatch_merge -d '{"enabled": false, "scope":"kv-cache-pool:us-west-2"}'
```

devops-bot: Deploy job queued: flag-toggle-job-3109876560 started on 3 hosts (canary).

leo (eng-runtime): Canary results: 3 hosts toggled, eviction_rate dropped ~40% within 60s, cuda malloc OOMs stopped on those hosts. Moving to pool.

anya (eng-sre): While rolling, doing quick hotpatch to cap merged batch token count at 1024 as a safety net. Applying config change: `contbatch.max_tokens=1024`.

matt (ml-infra): Command to set cap in runtime config store:
```
redwoodctl config set kv.contbatch.max_tokens 1024 --env production --pool kv-cache-pool:us-west-2
```

devops-bot: Config change applied to 24 hosts. Rolling restart not required for dynamic config.

leo (eng-runtime): Observed cluster-wide drop in combined batch size histogram. Memory pressure falling. Still seeing fragmentation on a subset of nodes where arena free lists are highly fragmented.

anya (eng-sre): For fragmented hosts, plan: 1) mark for graceful drain, 2) run allocator compaction job (`arena.compact=true`), 3) restart service to reclaim GPU memory.

sara (oncall): Starting node drain for 6 worst hosts. Draining one by one to avoid capacity cliffs. Runbook steps: `drain`, `wait for 95p dropped to baseline`, `reprovision if needed`.

leo (eng-runtime): Quick allocator hotfix PR ready: bound slab growth and reduce slab split aggression. Will roll to canary after the contbatch toggle fully rolled. PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/512

matt (ml-infra): We should also add a telemetry gauge for merged_batch_token_count and a log alert when any single merged batch > 2048 to catch regressions earlier.

pierre (customer-success): Communicated to affected customers: initial mitigation in progress, hotfix being applied, ETA ~30m for full pool stabilisation. They appreciate the proactive updates.

devops-bot: Node drain triggered: node-uw2-kv-07 -> cordon, drain-start.

anya (eng-sre): After draining and compaction on node-07: GPU memory reclaimed, fragmentation metric dropped ~70%. No further OOMs.

leo (eng-runtime): Rolling allocator hotfix to canary group of 4 hosts now. Monitoring.

sara (oncall): Quick check on customer impact: 5xx rate down 80% since toggle + cap. Still residual elevated latency for a small subset but trending down.

devops-bot: Hotfix deploy job 3109876820 succeeded on canary. Promoting to remaining pool with 5m pauses.

leo (eng-runtime): Hotfix promoted. Bulk compaction scheduled during maintenance window for deeply fragmented nodes to avoid extra restarts. Added automatic compaction to the quick-recovery path if eviction_rate > 3x baseline.

anya (eng-sre): Post-mitigation telemetry summary (preliminary): eviction_rate peaked at 6x, merged batch median jumped from 40 -> 600 tokens on effected hosts, after actions median down to ~60. CUDA malloc OOM count reduced to zero.

pierre (customer-success): Updated customers. No new high-severity escalations. One enterprise asked for a postmortem.

leo (eng-runtime): Action items before handoff: - finalise PR#512 tests and prepare rollback plan; - add merged_batch_token_count alert; - schedule offline compaction for nodes with frag>0.4; - update runbook with contbatch safety caps.

sara (oncall): Handoff to night oncall @anya in 45m. Current cluster stable, continue to monitor. If eviction_rate or OOMs reappear -> wakeup.

anya (eng-sre): Acknowledged, taking handoff. Will keep checks every 15m for next 2h and coordinate with eng-runtime if any regressions.

incident-bot: Incident severity reduced to P2. Start incident timeline capture: incident-3109876543.

sara (oncall): Thanks team. Good recovery. We'll follow up with a blameless postmortem and timeline.

leo (eng-runtime): Note for postmortem: root cause = contbatch merge heuristic lacked global token cap; secondary cause = allocator slab growth + fragmentation that surfaced under high merged-object churn.

anya (eng-sre): Logging closed for this thread. Adding links: PR512, config changes, telemetry dashboards, and customer messages to the incident doc.

pierre (customer-success): Will draft customer-facing summary and share in #customer-communications once incident doc ready.

devops-bot: Incident thread archived to incident-archive/3109876543 after handoff.
